text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: elevated KV miss rate and tail latency detected for tenant=aspensys on dedicated-pool-asp (vpc-prod-eu-west). Triggered at 2367001200 UTC. Auto-paging #incidents.

alex_g: Im on pager. Dashboard shows prefix hit-rate for /aspensys/* collapsed to ~92% misses, error volume up. Link: https://dash.redwood/kv/aspensys (internal)

samira: Tagging eng-runtime, eng-sre. Any recent config changes or deploys to that pool?

oliver_eng: No deploys in last 8h according to deploy-bot. Pulling runtime logs and cache metrics now.

tom_aspensys: We kicked off a heavy dedupe job at ~2350 UTC (customer-side) that queries small hot keys repeatedly. Could be correlated.

alex_g: That pattern matches KV cache pollution: many short-lived keys evicting hot entries. Also seeing prefetch traffic amplified by cache misses -> amplification loop.

lia_sre: Short timeline mitigations: (A) throttle inbound requests for tenant (rate-limit) (B) toggle tenant prefetch off (C) add tenant to isolated cache partition/quota. Which is fastest?

samira: Wed prefer to avoid a customer-side throttle without consent. Can we toggle prefetch remotely without restart?

oliver_eng: Yes. control-plane exposes per-tenant prefetch flag. Command to run:

```
redwoodctl tenants update aspensys --set prefetch.enabled=false
```

Its a non-disruptive rollout; nodes pick up change within ~20-45s.

alex_g: Executing the toggle now. Will observe hit/miss and p99.

oncall-bot: ACTION: prefetch disable requested. Change acknowledged by control-plane. Propagating to pool nodes.

oliver_eng: Control-plane confirms change applied to 8/8 nodes at 2367001260 UTC.

lia_sre: Network of metrics shows prefetch outbound drops immediately. Miss rate falling from 92% -> 55% within first minute.

alex_g: p50 latency improving; p99 still high (400-650ms) but trending down. Error rate trending to baseline.

tom_aspensys: Weve paused the dedupe job on our end. Appreciate the assist. Well coordinate a safe ramp plan.

samira: For resilience: recommend adding an isolation config so heavy prefix patterns by a tenant are partitioned. oliver, can runtime do on-the-fly partition assignment?

oliver_eng: We have a cache isolation mechanism. API:

```
redwoodctl cache isolate --tenant aspensys --quota 0.10
```

This adjusts eviction boundaries and assigns a reserved fraction. No node restart required, but its a dynamic config change and has tradeoffs for co-tenants.

alex_g: Id prefer to hold on isolation until we see stable metrics for 10m with prefetch off. If miss < 20% and p99 < 450ms we'll close active mitigation and open a follow-up for automation.

lia_sre: Current snapshot (2367001345 UTC): miss=16%, p50=55ms, p99=390ms, error-rate back to baseline. Marking mitigation successful for now.

samira: Filing follow-up INC ticket: INC-2026-ASP-01. Action items: eng-runtime to implement auto-detection + auto-isolate rule; devex to update runbook for per-tenant prefetch toggles; cust-eng to coordinate restart/ramp plan with aspensys.

oliver_eng: I'll prototype an auto-rule: if tenant outgoing prefetch > T and miss rate > M for > 60s then add to isolation map and notify oncall. Will open PR with tests.

lia_sre: Handoff: Im on until 0300 UTC. If it regresses escalate to eng-sre pager. Nice work all. :thumbsup:

alex_g: Closing active mitigation, leaving channel open for customer coordination and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation verified). Probable root cause: tenant batch traffic causing KV prefix cache pollution + prefetch amplification loop. Follow-ups logged in INC-2026-ASP-01.
